attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript written by my collaborator.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-cn8t2p01/call-df62e7c7091f47e09bcb5e962b46234b/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, shutil
for name in ('pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL'):
 print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
for name in ('pdftoppm','pdftotext','pdfinfo','gs','python3'):
 print(name,shutil.which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:',reader.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
 text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
 print(f'Page {i}: {len(text)} characters, {page.mediabox}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i} ===\\n'+Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').read_text() for i in range(1,len(reader.pages)+1)))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-21.txt tmp/pdfs/page-22.txt tmp/pdfs/page-23.txt tmp/pdfs/page-24.txt tmp/pdfs/page-25.txt tmp/pdfs/page-26.txt tmp/pdfs/page-27.txt'

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant robustness problem: learning an invariant predictor does not ensure reliability when its preferred predictive feature becomes unavailable. This motivation is particularly useful for vision settings involving occlusion or cropping.

H-CMNIST provides a controlled test of retaining predictive ability after removing an easy invariant cue. In Table 1, ASGDRO improves over GDRO from 57.53% to 66.62% with the spurious box present and from 61.44% to 69.17% on shape alone, providing encouraging evidence of additional feature learning.

The empirical evaluation is broad and shows useful improvements. Worst-group accuracy increases over reported GDRO results from 68.6% to 74.2% on CMNIST and from 87.2% to 91.0% on CelebA. The matched DPLCLIP experiments improve average DomainBed accuracy from 72.9% with GDRO to 74.0% with ASGDRO.

Combining adaptive sharpness-aware updates with group reweighting is practical and readily applicable to existing models. The appendix supplies substantial hyperparameter and model-selection information, repeated-seed results, and an explicit acknowledgment of the additional training cost.
weaknesses: Theorem 1 is false for its stated objective. In its own setting, take Z=(1,...,1), Y=1, and θ=λ with nonnegative coefficients summing to one. Then max_{||ε||₂≤ρ} R(λ+ε)=pρ²/2 for every λ, so a single-feature solution and the uniform mixture are equally optimal. Appendix A.4 unjustifiably introduces λ⊙∇R and treats a first-order approximation as an equality. This invalidates the central guarantee that the stated objective selects diverse invariant mechanisms.

The formal connection between SIL and parameter flatness contains additional unsupported steps. Joint conditional invariance in Definition 1 does not generally imply invariance for every feature subset. Equation 4 equates a maximum over selected invariant mechanisms with a maximum over an entire parameter ball, although the latter generally only upper-bounds the former. Low-risk interpolation paths do not establish low risk throughout that ball. These gaps limit the claimed generality of the framework.

The evaluated algorithm differs materially from the analyzed algorithm. Section 4.3 uses one perturbation computed from average empirical risk in every data experiment, while Algorithm 1 and the theory use environment-specific perturbations. Environment gradients can cancel, so the shared perturbation need not expose each environment's sharp directions. No approximation guarantee or direct comparison establishes that this substitution preserves the claimed mechanism.

The experiments support practical robustness more convincingly than the claimed SIL mechanism. Only H-CMNIST directly removes an invariant cue; the real-image evaluations do not measure robustness to selective feature removal. Larger Grad-CAM regions and smaller Hessian eigenvalues do not establish reliance on multiple independently predictive features. Because the optimizer primarily combines established ASAM and GroupDRO components, establishing this connection is important to the paper's distinctive contribution.

Reproducibility and attribution remain uneven despite the useful appendix. H-CMNIST split sizes and its validation/model-selection protocol are unspecified, and Appendix A.8 does not provide full training configurations for the additional WILDS experiments. Many central baseline results are imported from prior work, leaving matched tuning difficult to assess. These are secondary reservations; the incorrect central theorem and the disconnect between the claimed mechanism and evaluated implementation determine the weak-reject recommendation.
